pairing.title: Pair with your IDE

help.title: Pairing
help.text:
The QR code in the IDE's Remote Control window opens this page with a one-time code. The code never leaves the phone: it is removed from the address at once.

Compare the keys before you pair. The IDE key here must match the key in the Remote Control window. When the IDE asks you to approve this phone, it shows the phone key - it must match the one here.

After you approve, the phone and the IDE talk end-to-end encrypted through the relay, which only passes frames and cannot read them. Several IDEs can be paired with one phone.

An app added to the Home Screen keeps its own pairings, apart from Safari. To pair it, press and hold the link of the QR code in the camera, choose Copy Link and paste it on this screen.

machines.title: My IDEs

help.title: Remote Control
help.text:
Each IDE paired with this phone is listed here with its open and recent projects. Project folders never leave the computer: the phone knows a project by a key.

All queues, Accounts and Connectors belong to the whole IDE, not to one project.

To add an IDE, open Remote Control in Agentic Workstation and scan its QR code with the phone camera.

Forget removes the pairing keys from this phone and tells the IDE to release it, if the IDE is reachable now. Otherwise revoke the phone in the IDE's Remote Control window.

notifications.title: Notifications

help.title: Notifications
help.text:
When this phone is not looking, a paired IDE can wake it: a conversation asks for a permission, a question or a plan, stops with an error or hits a usage limit, a scenario asks a question or a queue stops. Tapping the notification opens that conversation, queue or run. A finished turn does not notify.

The text is encrypted on the computer for this phone only. The relay and the push service of your phone see that a notification was sent, not what it says.

Turn off stops notifications from every IDE paired with this phone.

project.title: Project

help.title: Project
help.text:
Conversations are grouped by provider. Each shows what it is doing now and since when: working, needs you (a permission, a question or a plan) or idle. Past conversations can be opened and continued, and Search conversations finds a message by its words or by asking Claude.

Scenarios shows the shelves, the schedule and past runs. Scenario queues run scenarios one after another, in their own worktree or in the project folder.

A recent project that is not open in the IDE shows its past conversations and its queues. Open in the IDE opens it as a tab, and then its conversations show up here.

help.title: Conversation
help.text:
The feed shows the end of the conversation as the IDE sees it, and updates live. Load earlier brings older messages from the IDE, a page at a time.

While Claude works, a new message waits in the IDE's queue and goes after the current turn. Send now gives a queued message to Claude right away: it reads it at its next step. Move up, Move down and Remove change the queue.

Stop next to the message field ends the turn. If Claude Code does not stop, Force stop ends its process; the unfinished work of the turn is lost. A running agent or background command can be stopped on its own from its line in the feed.

Ask aside asks Claude a side question about this conversation without stopping its work. The answer stays out of the chat and shows only on this phone.

Rewind next to your message takes the conversation back to it, and can put the code back too. The message text returns to the field.

A permission can be allowed once or denied. Allowing a tool always, bypass and auto modes, the terminal and ! commands are only available at the computer.

Tap a photo to see it large. A big photo comes reduced to fit the phone; the original stays in the IDE.

queue.title: Queue

help.title: Scenario queue
help.text:
A queue runs its scenarios one after another, in its own worktree or in the project folder.

Stop after current lets the running scenario finish, then the queue waits. A waiting item can stop the queue after itself, run only if the one before it succeeded, move up or down, or be removed. Clear waiting removes every waiting item at once; the running scenario and the finished ones stay.

Closing a queue and removing its worktree are only available at the computer.

run.title: Run

help.title: Scenario run
help.text:
A run is one pass of a scenario. Cards do the work, and the main thread (the head) reads what each card did and decides what comes next.

When the head asks you, answer here. Write to the head at the bottom: it reads your words between cards.

Pause keeps everything alive. Stop cuts the current card short. A stopped or failed run, or one waiting for a usage limit, can be continued.

help.title: Start a scenario
help.text:
Pick a scenario from the project shelf or your personal shelf and answer its questions.

A new queue in its own worktree works on a separate branch, and the project files stay as they are. Without a worktree it works in the project folder. An existing queue runs the scenario after what is already in it.

aside.title: Side questions

help.title: Side questions
help.text:
Claude answers a side question from this conversation without stopping its work. It does not read files or run tools, and neither the question nor the answer goes into the chat.

The answer comes only to this phone and stays here until the page is closed. An answer can take a few minutes.

search.title: Search conversations

help.title: Search conversations
help.text:
Find looks for the words you type in this project's conversations, the way the IDE search does. Put a phrase in quotes to find it as a whole.

Ask Claude reads the conversations and points at the places that fit a description, like what it was about or roughly when. It runs on its own and counts against your usage; Cancel stops it.

Tap a result to open that conversation. Search works only in a project that is open in the IDE.

scenarios.title: Scenarios

help.title: Scenarios
help.text:
The project shelf and your personal shelf, the scheduled runs and the past runs of this project.

Tap a scenario to read it, start it, schedule it, copy it or delete it. Write with AI describes a new scenario in words; Claude writes it and you save it to a shelf. Editing a scenario by hand is only available at the computer.

A scheduled run starts at its hour by the Mac's clock, while the IDE is open. Star a run to keep it easy to find; delete removes its record from the computer.

scenario.title: Scenario

help.title: Scenario
help.text:
The whole scenario as it is on the shelf: the questions it asks before it starts, the head that leads the run, and its stages with their cards. Tap a card to read its prompt.

Start runs it now; Schedule sets an hour for it. Duplicate puts a copy on the same shelf. Editing is only available at the computer, or write a new one with AI.

head.retries_other: Sends a card back up to {{count}} times

help.title: Schedule a run
help.text:
At its hour the scenario starts in a new queue, with the answers you give now: at that hour there is nobody to answer.

The hour is by the Mac's clock, not this phone's. A run starts only while the IDE is open; an hour that passed while it was closed shows as missed.

In its own worktree the run works on a separate branch, and the project files stay as they are.

draft.title: Write with AI

help.title: Write with AI
help.text:
Describe what the scenario should do: the work, the steps, when it is done. Claude writes the whole scenario in a few minutes, and you read it before saving.

Save to shelf saves exactly what Claude wrote. To change it, discard it and describe it again, or edit it at the computer. Leaving this screen while Claude writes cancels the draft.

accounts.title: Accounts

help.title: Accounts
help.text:
The Claude accounts signed in on the computer, and how much of each usage window is spent. Refresh brings fresh numbers.

Use this account switches the conversations to it: each one restarts on it as soon as it is free.

Forget removes an added account's sign-in from the Mac. Sign out signs Claude Code out of the default sign-in on every machine. Adding an account and signing in again need a browser at the Mac.

accounts.logoutTitle: Sign out of the default sign-in?
accounts.logoutText: This signs Claude Code out on every machine that uses this sign-in. Signing in again needs a browser at the Mac.

help.title: Connectors
help.text:
The apps the IDE connects to for Claude: mail, calendar, Notion, Slack and any MCP server. Each shows its state and how many of its tools are on.

Reconnect asks the service for its tools again and clears a lost sign-in if the key works again.

Adding, removing and signing in to a connector are only available at the computer: signing in needs a browser at the Mac.
